dim_resolution.method: linear scan kind.off/kind.dat (rows=4); store row index i; complete_cast.subject_id/status_id are 1-based ids, so compare against (i+1)
linear scan info.off/info.dat (rows=113); compare child info_type_id against (i+1)
linear scan keyword.off/keyword.dat (rows=134170); push back (i+1) on match

driver.notes: Single sequential scan of complete_cast (135K rows). Dedup distinct mv set sized ~17879.

join_order.notes: Most selective per-mv probe — run first. For each mv, scan slot [mkoff[mv], mkoff[mv+1]); break on first keyword_id in k_ids.

For each mv slot, scan rows; if info_type_id==it1_id AND info in genre_set: capture info string_view for MIN(mi.info); track local min and continue scanning to find smallest genre string for this movie? No — for MIN aggregation we only need one matching row to exist (qualifies movie), and we MIN across qualifying values. So MIN is over the matched info strings. Keep running global min.

join_order.build: note_set flat_hash_set<string_view> (5 writer notes) + gender array
join_order.probe: cast_info via offsets[mv]; deref person_id -> name.gender[pid-1]
join_order.notes: For each mv slot in cast_info, check note ∈ note_set (length prefilter [6..15]); if match, fetch pid, check gender[pid-1]==m_code; on success capture name.name via name.name.off/dat[pid-1] for MIN.
For each mv slot in mi_idx, find any row with info_type_id==it2_id; capture mi_idx.info string for MIN. Least selective — run last.

data_structures.genre_set: flat_hash_set<std::string_view> (6 elements, length prefilter min=3 max=8)
data_structures.note_set: flat_hash_set<std::string_view> (5 elements, length prefilter min=8 max=15)
data_structures.agg_state: per-thread {min_mi_info, min_mi_idx_info, min_name, min_title} as std::string_view + owning buffer not needed (mmap-backed)

indexes.purpose: not used as parent index — driver is full scan of complete_cast columns

parallelism.notes: Driver scan of complete_cast is single-threaded (135K rows, fast). Per-mv probe loop is parallelised; each thread maintains local MIN strings and merges under a single mutex at end.

aggregation.min_semantics: lexicographic on raw bytes; only update if mv qualifies on all four semi-join predicates (mk, mi, ci, mi_idx). MIN values may come from different mvs since aggregates are unrelated.
aggregation.qualification_rule: Per IMDB-JOB semantics: a row in the cartesian product contributes to MIN. Therefore only mvs satisfying all semi-joins contribute; for those mvs, every qualifying (mi_row × ci_writer_male_row × mi_idx_row) combination contributes — but for MIN we can simply track the min over ALL qualifying mi.info strings for qualifying mvs, and similarly for mi_idx.info, n.name (over all qualifying writer-male persons of qualifying mvs), and t.title (over qualifying mvs).

memory_estimate.mmap_pages_touched: complete_cast(3 cols × 135K × 4B = ~1.6MB), per-mv probes across mk/mi/mii/ci slot ranges + name.gender(4MB) + name.name.off/dat (sparse)
memory_estimate.fits_in_l3: working set dominated by mv probes; random access into ci/mi/mi_idx; HDD prefetch helps via sequential slot access within a movie
